title: FIU pedestrian bridge: node 11/12 design error, peer-review failure, cracking response, and road exposure
summary: FIU is encoded as a design-review, crack-signal interpretation, and public-exposure governance case: the bridge span failed at node 11/12 while the road underneath remained open.

status_history.note: Added as civil/structural failure lane record.

claims.claim: The NTSB investigation page records the March 15, 2018 catastrophic failure at node 11/12 of the FIU pedestrian bridge while retensioning work was underway; the 174-foot span fell onto the roadway and six people died.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The NTSB probable-cause statement identifies load/capacity calculation errors made by the bridge designer as the probable cause.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The NTSB probable-cause statement also identifies an inadequate peer review, failure to recognize the significance of cracking, and failure to close the road under the bridge before collapse.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The record is encoded as a design-review plus hazard-exposure failure because crack evidence and peer review did not convert into effective stop/closure authority before the public roadway remained exposed.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

type_payload.system: concrete pedestrian bridge span, node 11/12, design check, peer review, construction/traffic exposure controls

sequence_of_events.event: Pedestrian bridge span was placed over an active roadway.
Cracking and retensioning context developed near node 11/12.
Span failed catastrophically at node 11/12 while roadway beneath remained open.
NTSB traced design-calculation, peer-review, cracking-response, and road-closure failures.

type_payload.proximate_cause: Load/capacity calculation errors at node 11/12 in the bridge design.
contributing_factors: work/closure governance failure with public road exposed
latent_conditions: public exposure depended on correct interpretation of structural distress
independent review did not catch critical design error
stop-work/road-closure threshold did not function before collapse
